title: Short Stuff: Habsburg Jaw
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Habsburg jaw. Josh and Chuck cover the Habsburg dynasty's rise from Rudolph I's election as Roman-German king in the 13th century, the conquest of Austria after Ottokar's death, territorial expansion through conquest and marriage (including Maximilian's marriage to Mary of Burgundy), and the family's distinctive prominent lower jaw. They explain the medical term mandibular prognathism, mention mandibular deficiency, quote a 17th-century account of Charles II of Spain struggling to chew, and attribute the trait to inbreeding, citing geneticist Gregory Montgomery Slatkin's remarks on recessive traits.

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to the Habsburgs
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the Habsburg jaw and introduce the Habsburg family as a long-ruling European dynasty.

segments.title: Rise of the Habsburgs
segments.summary: Rudolph I becomes Roman-German king in the 13th century, rivalry with Ottokar leads to the Habsburg takeover of Austria, and the family expands through conquest and marriage, including Maximilian's marriage to Mary of Burgundy.

segments.title: Description of the Habsburg jaw
segments.summary: The hosts describe the distinctive prominent lower jaw and underbite associated with the Habsburgs, and suggest looking up images of Habsburg portraits.

segments.title: Medical terms and the Charles II account
segments.summary: The jaw is medically called mandibular prognathism, with mandibular deficiency also noted. A 17th-century account of Charles II of Spain describes his inability to chew and swallowing food whole.

segments.title: Inbreeding and the origin of the jaw
segments.summary: The hosts attribute the Habsburg jaw to inbreeding within the family, explaining how recessive genes become more likely to appear in closely related couples' children, and cite geneticist Gregory Montgomery Slatkin.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the episode and give the show credits.
